channel.title: viaduct.sh articles
channel.description: Updates and notes from the viaduct project.

item.title: Name your own tunnel
item.description: viaduct handed out random names on purpose. Now you can request a specific subdomain with --name, pinned if it is free.

item.title: Why I built my own reverse tunnel
item.description: ngrok was my default for years, with localtunnel and Pinggy alongside it. I built my own anyway, and the tunnelling turned out to be the easy part.

item.title: Idle tunnels stay ready
item.description: A tunnel you leave open but unused now stays live, so the first request after a quiet spell loads straight away instead of hanging.

item.title: Protect a tunnel with a password, a token, or an IP allowlist
item.description: Tunnels are public by default. Now you can gate one with Basic auth, a bearer token, or an IP allowlist, checked at the edge so an unwanted request never reaches your machine.

item.title: Inspect your traffic live, no restart
item.description: The traffic inspector now toggles on and off with a single key on a running tunnel, no reconnect and no new URL.

item.title: Welcome to viaduct.sh
item.description: viaduct.sh is a free, open-source reverse tunnel: one command gives a service on your machine a public HTTPS URL, no inbound ports or NAT configuration required.
